bull.b: The large recurring contribution from instruments, accessories, and service creates revenue visibility beyond system placements. As the installed base and procedure volumes expand, this model can support durable cash generation and deepen customer relationships over multiple years.

High operating margins and rapidly growing free cash flow provide substantial internal funding for research, customer support, and market expansion. Strong cash conversion also improves resilience and gives management flexibility to sustain investment through changing procedure or capital cycles.

A growing installed base reinforces Intuitive's ecosystem because each additional system can generate future procedures, recurring consumables, and service revenue. Continued development across da Vinci 5, SP, XiR, and ION also broadens applications and supports adoption across care settings.

bear.b: The slowing growth profile indicates that Intuitive may be moving beyond its earlier post-2021 acceleration, making future expansion more dependent on new indications, product adoption, and procedure growth. Lower growth can also reduce operating leverage and make execution more important.

China-related tender weakness and domestic competition can constrain system placements, pricing, and near-term procedure expansion in an important international market. The fact that da Vinci 5 is not yet cleared there may further limit product momentum until regulatory access improves.

bear.t: Extended-use instruments may reduce recurring revenue
bear.b: If instruments are used for longer periods, customers may purchase fewer replacements per procedure, weakening the recurring revenue economics that support the razor-and-blades model. The uncertain rollout and magnitude make future instrument revenue and margin effects harder to assess.
